headline: Workers find $10 million in buried gold

sources.title: Construction workers find gold stash worth $10 million in Belgium (CBS News)
Construction workers in Belgium uncover $10 million in gold at work (CNN)
$10 million gold treasure discovered during renovation of Belgian brewery (WSB-TV)
Workers discover gold bars and coins worth $10 million at former brewery (video, CBS News)

chunks.text: It started as a normal workday in Dendermonde, a town in the Belgian region of East Flanders. A construction [[crew]] was digging under an old building, once home to a [[brewery]], to lay new [[sewer pipes]]. Then a worker's [[drill]] {{broke through}} an old [[cellar]] wall, and something yellow appeared in the dust. While doing one of the least [[glamorous]] jobs in construction, the crew had {{come across}} it [[by pure chance]]: a [[fortune]] in gold.

verbs.correct: To make a hole in something
verbs.why: Firefighters can break through a locked door in seconds, and morning sun can break through thick clouds after a storm. Here a worker's drill broke through an old cellar wall, and something gold appeared in the dust.

verbs.wrong: To dig for something for years
verbs.why: You come across an old coin while cleaning a drawer, or come across a forgotten letter tucked inside a book. Here a construction crew came across a fortune in gold completely by chance while laying new pipes.

chunks.text: The [[find]] was huge: about 50 gold bars and pile after pile of old gold coins, [[hidden]] inside the walls. Together, the [[treasure]] {{comes to}} about nine million euros, or more than ten million dollars. The news {{got out}} fast, and photos of the shining bars soon appeared on the local police's own Facebook page.

verbs.why: A restaurant bill can come to sixty dollars with tax, and repair costs sometimes come to more than the car is worth. Together, this hidden gold comes to about nine million euros, or more than ten million dollars.

verbs.wrong: To stay quiet for a while
verbs.why: A secret can get out before anyone plans to share it, and word can get out about a surprise party days too early. Here the news got out fast, and photos of the shining gold bars soon appeared on the local police's own page.

chunks.text: The workers did not [[think twice]]. They called the police [[at once]] and {{handed over}} [[every last]] coin to the [[officers]]. Nobody tried to {{walk off with}} a fortune in their pockets. The treasure was moved to a high-security government [[vault]], where it is now {{locked away}}. The building [[site]] itself has been {{fenced off}}, and police warned [[treasure hunters]] that digging there would be [[pointless]].

verbs.why: A cashier hands over the keys at the end of a shift, and an honest stranger hands over a lost wallet to the front desk. These workers called the police right away and handed over every last coin they found.

A careless guest can walk off with a hotel umbrella, and a stranger can walk off with an unattended bag at a cafe. Nobody on this crew tried to walk off with even a single coin from the gold they found.

verbs.correct: To keep something in a safe place
verbs.wrong: To melt something into new bars
verbs.why: A museum locks away its rarest coins overnight, and careful people lock away important papers in a safe. This treasure is now locked away in a high-security government vault, far from any risk.

verbs.correct: To close an area with a barrier
verbs.wrong: To search an area with dogs
verbs.why: A city can fence off a broken playground until repairs are done, and a farmer can fence off a field to protect the sheep. Here police fenced off the whole building site and warned treasure hunters that more digging would be pointless.

chunks.text: One question remains: who does the gold {{belong to}}? The building is owned today by a local [[charity]], but nobody knows who hid the treasure, or when. Old [[records]] about the house might {{clear up}} the [[mystery]]. If the original owner's family never {{turns up}}, the [[courts]] will have to decide. For now, no one can say where the gold will finally {{end up}}, but everyone agrees on one thing: the workers who found it did [[the right thing]].

verbs.why: This old jacket belongs to my younger brother, and the land by the river belongs to the whole town. Right now, nobody can say for certain who the gold truly belongs to, since the original owner is unknown.

A short phone call can clear up a simple mix-up, and new evidence can clear up a mystery that lasted years. Old property records about the building might finally clear up who hid this fortune, and when.

verbs.wrong: To ask for a big reward
verbs.why: A lost cat can turn up two streets away days later, and an old friend can turn up unannounced after many years. If the original owner's family never turns up, the courts will have to decide who keeps the gold.

verbs.wrong: To be sold at an auction
verbs.why: Leftover cake can end up in the trash by the next morning, and an old trophy can end up forgotten in a garage box. Nobody can say yet where this gold will finally end up, but everyone agrees the workers did the right thing.

mainIdea.s: Workers laying sewer pipes in a Belgian town found gold bars and coins worth about ten million dollars. They called the police and handed everything over at once.
mainIdea.why: A crew in Dendermonde came across about 50 gold bars and piles of coins, worth about nine million euros, and gave it all to the police.

mainIdea.s: Workers in Belgium found millions in buried gold and got to keep it as their reward. The happy crew shared about fifty bars and many piles of rare old coins.
mainIdea.why: Close, but the workers kept nothing. They handed the gold to the police, and it is locked away while the owner is unknown.

mainIdea.s: A museum in Belgium has opened a big new show about pirate treasure from old ships. Visitors can hold real gold bars and try a metal detector in the garden.
mainIdea.why: The article is about construction workers finding hidden gold under a building, not about a museum show.

lines.text: Construction workers in Belgium found ten million dollars in gold under an old building. And gave every coin to the police.
Every last coin. The crew was digging under a former brewery to lay sewer pipes when a drill {{broke through}} an old cellar wall, and something yellow appeared in the dust.
About 50 gold bars and piles of old coins hidden inside the walls. Together the treasure {{comes to}} about nine million euros. They {{came across}} it [[by pure chance]].
And nobody tried to {{walk off with}} even a little?
Nobody. They called the police at once and {{handed over}} everything. The gold is now {{locked away}} in a high-security government vault.
The news {{got out}} fast, photos even appeared on the police's own Facebook page. The site has been {{fenced off}}, and police warned treasure hunters that digging there is pointless.
So who does the gold {{belong to}}?
